anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the SS2040FL U6 is drawn with its anode (pin 1, the side facing the 'BAT+' label) tied to the BAT+ rail and its cathode (pin 2) tied to the battery positive (U7 pin 1 / Net-(U6-A)). The diode therefore points from BAT+ toward the cell.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the battery feed is 'U7 pin 1 -> Net-(U6-A) -> U6 (SS2040FL) anode->cathode -> BAT+', i.e. the anode must be on the battery side and the cathode on BAT+, so the cell supplies BAT+ and BAT+ cannot back-feed into the raw 18650.

evidence.quote: Battery (U7, 18650 holder) → pin 1 → Net-(U6-A) → U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+. ... the diode's evident function is to prevent USB/adapter 5 V from back-feeding current into the raw, uncontrolled 18650 cell
EthernetAndPower.kicad_sch, page 3/4, bottom-left: U6 SS2040FL with pin 1 adjacent to the 'BAT+' label and pin 2 running to U7 (Keystone 1043) pin 1

anomalies.impact: The 18650 cannot power the board (the series diode is reverse-biased for battery->BAT+ current). Conversely, when USB or the DC barrel jack is present, 5 V on BAT+ forward-biases U6 into the uncontrolled cell, back-feeding / uncontrolled-charging the battery - the exact hazard the diode was intended to prevent.

parsed.summary: The battery-isolation diode U6 (SS2040FL) appears installed/reversed relative to the specification: its anode sits on BAT+ and its cathode on the cell, so the 18650 cannot feed the board and external 5 V can back-feed into the raw cell, defeating the diode's documented purpose.
